Four query vectors attend across those summaries, then project down to one logit. Confidence is the lower of that score and the decoder's own probability. Both have to agree. The head reads the backbone under stop gradient. Training it cannot move one weight of the model it judges. It was trained in a separate run and merged in afterwards. No gradient path reaches it. nvfp4-kv-cache.transcript: Hi, I'm Holly! SGLang can now keep its KV cache in four bits. Here's how. Plus an eight-bit scale, shared by a block of B values. Set it equal to point five six two five, and B comes out as exactly sixteen. The scale is already counted. Prefill computes in FP8, then packs keys and values into one pool: four-bit values, and a scale per sixteen. Decode reads the four-bit cache directly. Fewer bytes per step: twenty-six to thirty percent more throughput at the same batch. Chunked prefill expands the cached prefix back into FP8, so prefill gets no speedup. Here is the post's own figure: one shared memory pool in the middle, and three attention paths around it. Inside the pool: packed four-bit values, one block scale per sixteen elements, and a per-layer global scale. The benchmarked model has sixty-four layers. Forty-eight are gated DeltaNet, holding a fixed-size state the flag never touches. Only the sixteen full-attention layers keep a per-token cache: thirty-two kibibytes a token in FP8, eighteen in four-bit. The 1.78x is a property of the cache pool, not the GPU: weights and workspace don't shrink. To recap: four-bit values with a scale per sixteen, a faster decode, and a cache only full attention keeps. No per-layer structure. In the three smaller files, blocks zero, one, sixty-three and sixty-four keep the primary type. Blocks two to sixty-two crush their gate and up weights. Same keep-set at three budgets. A knapsack re-solved per budget would not normally do that; a first-and-last rule would. voxel-tto.transcript: Hi, I'm Parsley! When poses drift, feed-forward Gaussian splatting fails quietly: input views look fine, new views don't. Here's VoxelTTO's fix. where-to-use-jev.transcript: Hi, I'm Kumquat! A decision model like Jev never writes: it picks from a list you send. Here's where it fits.
